samuel2.13.p1.b1.text: After some time, David’s son Amnon fell in love with Tamar, the beautiful sister of David’s son Absalom.

samuel2.13.p1.b2.text: Amnon was sick with frustration over his sister Tamar, …

samuel2.13.p1.b3.text: “Why are you, the son of the king, so depressed morning after morning?”

samuel2.13.p1.b4.text: “I am in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.”

samuel2.13.p2.b1.text: “Lie down on your bed and pretend you are ill. When your father comes to see you, say to him, …”

samuel2.13.p2.b2.text: “Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of cakes in my sight, so that I may eat from her hand.”

samuel2.13.p2.b3.text: “Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare a meal for him.”

samuel2.13.p3.b1.text: So Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon, who was lying down. She took some dough, kneaded it, made cakes in his sight, and baked them.

samuel2.13.p3.b3.text: Tamar took the cakes she had made and went to her brother Amnon’s bedroom.

samuel2.13.p4.b1.text: And when she had brought them to him to eat, …

samuel2.13.p4.b2.text: “No, my brother! … Do not humiliate me, for such a thing should never be done in Israel. Do not do this disgraceful thing!”

samuel2.13.p4.b3.text: “Please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you.”

samuel2.13.p4.b4.text: But Amnon refused to listen to her, …

samuel2.13.p5.b1.text: Then Amnon hated Tamar with such intensity that his hatred was greater than the love he previously had.

samuel2.13.p5.b2.text: “No, … sending me away is worse than this great wrong you have already done to me!”

samuel2.13.p5.b3.text: “Throw this woman out and bolt the door behind her!”

samuel2.13.p5.b4.text: So Amnon’s attendant threw her out and bolted the door behind her. Now Tamar was wearing a robe of many colors, because this is what the king’s virgin daughters wore.

samuel2.13.p6.b1.text: And Tamar put ashes on her head and tore her robe. And putting her hand on her head, she went away crying bitterly.

samuel2.13.p6.b2.text: “Has your brother Amnon been with you? Be quiet for now, my sister. He is your brother. …”

samuel2.13.p6.b3.text: So Tamar lived as a desolate woman in the house of her brother Absalom.

samuel2.13.p7.b1.text: When King David heard all this, he was furious.

samuel2.13.p7.b2.text: And Absalom never said a word to Amnon, either good or bad, because he hated Amnon for disgracing his sister Tamar.

samuel2.13.p8.b1.text: Two years later, when Absalom’s sheepshearers were at Baal-hazor near Ephraim, he invited all the sons of the king.

samuel2.13.p8.b2.text: “No, my son, … we should not all go, or we would be a burden to you.”

samuel2.13.p8.b3.text: “If not, … please let my brother Amnon go with us.”

samuel2.13.p8.b4.text: But Absalom urged him, so the king sent Amnon and the rest of his sons.

samuel2.13.p9.b1.text: “Watch Amnon until his heart is merry with wine, … Be courageous and valiant!”

samuel2.13.p9.b2.text: So Absalom’s young men did to Amnon just as Absalom had ordered.

samuel2.13.p9.b3.text: Then all the other sons of the king got up, and each one fled on his mule.

samuel2.13.p10.b1.text: “Absalom has struck down all the sons of the king; not one of them is left!”

samuel2.13.p10.b2.text: Then the king stood up, tore his clothes, and lay down on the ground; and all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.

samuel2.13.p10.b3.text: “My lord must not think they have killed all the sons of the king, for only Amnon is dead.”

samuel2.13.p10.b4.text: “In fact, Absalom has planned this since the day Amnon violated his sister Tamar.”

samuel2.13.p11.b1.text: When the young man standing watch looked up, he saw many people coming down the road west of him, along the side of the hill.

samuel2.13.p11.b2.text: And as he finished speaking, the sons of the king came in, wailing loudly. Then the king and all his servants also wept very bitterly.

samuel2.13.p11.b3.text: After Absalom had fled and gone to Geshur, he stayed there three years.

samuel2.13.p11.b4.text: And King David longed to go to Absalom, for he had been consoled over Amnon’s death.
